title: Axiomatic set theory: sets, classes, and the axioms of ZF
summary: The axioms justify familiar set constructions while excluding a set containing everything.
abstract: Can there be a set of all sets? Trying to form the collection of sets that do not contain themselves leads to Russell’s paradox, so unrestricted set formation cannot be allowed. Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory replaces it with explicit axioms: subsets are taken from an existing set, and other axioms build pairs, power sets, and sets of values. These rules still support familiar mathematical constructions, including numbers and functions. They also explain why the collection of all sets can be described as a class but cannot itself be a set.
